title: Memory, networks & power
summary: DRAM and NAND cells, HBM stacks, cluster networks and the energy of every token.

then: Computing lives in mainframes, minicomputers and PCs.
Web companies build large data centers from ordinary PC servers.
Cloud computing (from 2006) puts servers in giant shared data centers.
GPU clusters linked by NVLink (from 2016) and fast networks train AI models.

challenges.title: What does power really cost AI?
challenges.task: Double the price of electricity on the map and see how far the cost of an AI answer moves.

learn.plain: An AI chip is like a giant factory that needs constant deliveries. Memory chips are the warehouses next door, the network is the road system between factories, and the power plant keeps the lights on. If any of them can't keep up, the factory sits idle.
learn.engineer: DRAM retention scales roughly 2× per 10 °C, so refresh (tREFI 3.9 µs, tRFC hundreds of ns) costs a few percent of bandwidth. 3D NAND scales by layer count (286–400+ layers, multi-deck channel-hole etch, CMOS bonded to array) and bits per cell, trading endurance and read margin. HBM4 doubles the interface to 2,048 bits; stack height within 775 µm forces die thinning and pushes hybrid bonding for 16- to 20-high. Scale-up fabrics (NVLink 6 at 3.6 TB/s per GPU) versus scale-out at 1.6 Tb/s per GPU shape parallelism; optics power and PUE shape joules per token.

quiz.q: Why must DRAM be refreshed constantly?
options: Its tiny capacitors leak charge within milliseconds to seconds
quiz.why: Every row is rewritten at least every 64 ms (32 ms when hot) before the weakest cells fade.

quiz.q: Why do taller HBM stacks push the industry toward hybrid bonding?
options: The stack must fit a fixed height, and removing the bump gap leaves room for thicker, stronger dies
It makes memory faster to manufacture
It removes the need for TSVs
quiz.why: At 16 to 20 dies, micro-bump gaps would force dies thinner than is practical.

options: Total facility power divided by the power used by the IT equipment
quiz.why: A PUE of 1.2 means 20% extra power for cooling and conversion losses.
